title: Autonomy
coreMove: Engagement rises when clear goals remain in place while people gain real choice over how work is shaped and pursued.

exampleSpecs.audience: Jun, a clinic coordinator giving staff bounded time choice
exampleSpecs.stakes: A scheduling board must protect patient care while reducing needless control.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show one of the four Ts changing under clear standards.

exampleSpecs.audience: Calla, an engineering lead opening task choice
exampleSpecs.stakes: A roadmap review needs ownership without abandoning commitments.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use task autonomy within a shared roadmap.

exampleSpecs.audience: Ronan, a service manager moving from presence to outcomes
exampleSpecs.stakes: A remote team is being judged by green status dots instead of customer resolution.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply results-only thinking to a service environment.

exampleSpecs.audience: Yvette, a faculty lead giving technique choice
exampleSpecs.stakes: Teachers share a literacy goal but are being handed a script for every minute.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show technique autonomy under a common learning aim.

exampleSpecs.audience: Briar, a creative director leaving room in a brief
exampleSpecs.stakes: An agency brief is so scripted that the team can only decorate the answer.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show autonomy over technique in creative work.

exampleSpecs.audience: Keaton, a plant manager giving team choice for one experiment
exampleSpecs.stakes: An improvement huddle needs participation without losing safety rules.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use team autonomy in a bounded operational experiment.
